method: Read under subscription in the operator's browser and PARAPHRASED. No AMH passage is reproduced and no source_text is stored; every claim carries a locator and verdict licensed_source_not_quoted. Dose claims flagged dose:true. Apomorphine, safinamide, opicapone, benzatropine and domperidone are named in the topic but their monographs were NOT retrieved and no dose is reconstructed for them. AMH does not resolve whether motor complications reflect levodopa duration or disease progression, and that is recorded as evidence_unsettled rather than decided.

claims.claim: In Parkinson's disease there is dopaminergic deficiency and relative cholinergic excess, and drugs act by increasing dopamine or acting as dopamine agonists or anticholinergics
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: No agent has been proven to slow progression of Parkinson's disease and drug treatment provides symptomatic relief
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: The decision to begin drug treatment depends on the patient's situation and expectations and may be deferred until symptoms become physically or socially disabling
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: When tremor is the main symptom other conditions such as hyperthyroidism or essential tremor should be considered, and idiopathic Parkinson's disease must be distinguished from other causes of parkinsonism including drug-induced parkinsonism
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Levodopa or a dopamine agonist are the drugs of choice for initial treatment, with evidence suggesting no long-term advantage to starting with an agonist, so either is appropriate first line, individualised on severity, comorbidities, adverse effects and preference
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Treatment starts at a low dose and increases gradually to improve mobility while minimising adverse effects
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Levodopa is the most effective drug for motor symptoms, improving bradykinesia and rigidity and less consistently tremor, and is first line for most people especially the elderly and those with cognitive impairment
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Levodopa is given with a peripheral dopa decarboxylase inhibitor, carbidopa or benserazide, to reduce peripheral metabolism, allowing lower levodopa doses and fewer peripheral adverse effects such as nausea, vomiting and hypotension
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Long-term levodopa is associated with increased motor fluctuations including end-of-dose failure and on-off effect, dyskinesias and dystonias, which may relate to duration of treatment and or reflect disease progression
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Device-assisted therapy such as levodopa with carbidopa intestinal gel infusion or foslevodopa with foscarbidopa subcutaneous infusion may be considered for levodopa-responsive patients with severe disabling motor fluctuations not controlled by oral therapy
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Oral dopamine agonists include bromocriptine and cabergoline as ergot derivatives and pramipexole which is not ergot-derived, and they improve bradykinesia and rigidity but are less effective than levodopa
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Dopamine agonists may cause confusion and hallucinations more often than levodopa, especially in the elderly, people with dementia, or at high doses
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: As monotherapy in early disease dopamine agonists delay onset of motor fluctuations and dyskinesias and may be preferred to levodopa in younger patients, but long-term monotherapy is limited by adverse effects including impulse control disorders
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Adding a dopamine agonist to levodopa improves motor fluctuations and allows the levodopa dose to be reduced
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Efficacy of oral dopamine agonists is broadly similar but pramipexole is preferred because it is not associated with the rare fibrotic complications of ergot derivatives, and bromocriptine is rarely used
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Rotigotine is a non-ergot dopamine agonist used as monotherapy or with levodopa and, being a patch, may suit patients unwilling or unable to take oral therapy such as those with swallowing difficulties
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Apomorphine is useful in people severely disabled by motor fluctuations refractory to conventional treatment, may allow levodopa reduction, is started in hospital under specialist supervision by intermittent subcutaneous injection or continuous infusion, and is highly emetogenic requiring domperidone pretreatment
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: MAO-B inhibitors rasagiline, safinamide and selegiline are mainly adjuncts to levodopa in later disease with similar efficacy to entacapone in reducing off time but less than oral dopamine agonists, and rasagiline or rarely selegiline may be used as initial monotherapy in mild symptoms being less effective but possibly better tolerated
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: COMT inhibitors entacapone and opicapone are adjuncts to levodopa for end-of-dose motor fluctuations, increasing on time but also increasing levodopa-induced dyskinesias and gastrointestinal adverse effects, and the levodopa dose may need reducing
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Amantadine has dopaminergic and anticholinergic activity, is more effective than anticholinergics for akinesia and rigidity but less for tremor, loses some efficacy after 3 to 6 months, and is mainly used in later disease for drug-induced dyskinesias or as monotherapy for tremor in early disease
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Anticholinergics benzatropine and trihexyphenidyl are used infrequently because of adverse effects and poor efficacy, should be avoided in the elderly and those with cognitive impairment, have modest effect on tremor and little on rigidity and bradykinesia, and must be withdrawn slowly to avoid precipitating a cholinergic crisis
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Deep brain stimulation may benefit selected patients with inadequately controlled motor fluctuations or dyskinesia despite optimised drug therapy, or drug-refractory tremor, with specialist advice
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Non-motor symptoms of Parkinson's disease include autonomic dysfunction such as orthostatic hypotension, constipation, neurogenic bladder disturbance and sexual dysfunction, sleep disorders including REM-sleep behaviour disorder, depression, anxiety, cognitive decline and eventually dementia, sensory complaints and pain
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Psychosis is rare in untreated Parkinson's disease and appears predominantly drug induced, with levodopa less likely to cause it than other antiparkinsonian drugs
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: For drug-induced psychosis, reduce antiparkinsonian drugs where possible especially dopamine agonists and anticholinergics and consider levodopa monotherapy, then if symptoms persist use low-dose quetiapine or clozapine which are less likely than other antipsychotics to worsen parkinsonism
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Treatment of dementia in Parkinson's disease with anticholinesterases may be of some benefit
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Domperidone is preferred for nausea because it does not cross the blood-brain barrier and is not expected to worsen parkinsonism, while prochlorperazine and metoclopramide should be avoided because of central dopamine antagonist activity
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Abrupt withdrawal of some antiparkinsonian drugs has been associated with symptoms resembling neuroleptic malignant syndrome including fever, muscle rigidity, rhabdomyolysis and profuse sweating, so doses should be reduced gradually
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Dopaminergic drugs particularly dopamine agonists commonly cause impulse control disorders, and patients and carers should be warned and behaviour monitored
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: There is no evidence-based strategy for additional agents in later Parkinson's disease because few trials directly compare the classes used as adjuncts
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Somnolence and episodes of sudden sleep have been reported with all dopamine agonists, levodopa and rasagiline, may be caused by the disease or exacerbated by dopaminergic drugs, it is unclear whether some drugs are worse or how to identify those at risk, and affected patients should be advised not to drive or operate machinery
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Parkinson's disease' (Neurological drugs > Drugs for parkinsonism), July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Levodopa dosage is expressed as levodopa; conventional products start at oral 50 to 100 mg 2 or 3 times daily adjusted gradually, and up to 2 g daily in 3 or more doses may be needed
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monographs levodopa with benserazide/carbidopa, pramipexole, rotigotine, rasagiline, entacapone, amantadine, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Nausea and vomiting may occur with the low levodopa doses used at initiation because dopa decarboxylase inhibition may be insufficient
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monographs levodopa with benserazide/carbidopa, pramipexole, rotigotine, rasagiline, entacapone, amantadine, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Pramipexole conventional tablets start at 125 micrograms 3 times daily for a week, then 250 micrograms 3 times daily for a week, then 500 micrograms 3 times daily, increasing weekly if needed by 250 micrograms 3 times daily to a maximum of 1.5 mg 3 times daily
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monographs levodopa with benserazide/carbidopa, pramipexole, rotigotine, rasagiline, entacapone, amantadine, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Pramipexole in renal impairment starts at 125 micrograms twice daily with a maximum of 2.25 mg daily for CrCl 20 to 50 mL per minute, and 125 micrograms once daily with a maximum of 1.5 mg daily for CrCl under 20 mL per minute
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monographs levodopa with benserazide/carbidopa, pramipexole, rotigotine, rasagiline, entacapone, amantadine, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Rasagiline is oral 1 mg once daily, and as an adjunct the levodopa dose may need reducing if dopaminergic adverse effects such as dyskinesia occur
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monographs levodopa with benserazide/carbidopa, pramipexole, rotigotine, rasagiline, entacapone, amantadine, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Entacapone is oral 200 mg with each levodopa-carbidopa or levodopa-benserazide dose to a maximum of 2 g daily, and the daily levodopa dose may need a 10 to 30 percent reduction to reduce dopaminergic adverse effects
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monographs levodopa with benserazide/carbidopa, pramipexole, rotigotine, rasagiline, entacapone, amantadine, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Amantadine for Parkinson's disease in those 65 years and under is oral 100 mg once daily, increased after at least a week to 100 mg twice daily and if necessary after a further week to 100 mg 3 times daily which increases adverse effect risk, while those over 65 take 100 mg once daily
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monographs levodopa with benserazide/carbidopa, pramipexole, rotigotine, rasagiline, entacapone, amantadine, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Rotigotine in early stage Parkinson's disease starts as one 2 mg per 24 hours patch
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monographs levodopa with benserazide/carbidopa, pramipexole, rotigotine, rasagiline, entacapone, amantadine, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22
